Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 2220-3169), a developer test and CI procedure document. No executable code, authentication, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data-exposure logic changed in the supplied text.

Security-relevant content in the docs:

These support the T-041 mitigations (AES-GCM AAD authentication, tamper leads to delete and recompute). The documented tests use in-memory KEKs and temporary directories, and the doc states they do not exercise a hardware-backed key.
- Status canonical bytes tests (lines 2675-2684): Swift and Go golden vectors for nested-map ordering, relevant to TB-009 status-signature canonicalization.
- Fixture, CLI sandbox and benchmark guidance (lines 2632-2646): production endpoints, tokens, fan writes, sudo and Keychain are disallowed in tests. Persistent-key benchmark phases use an isolated key namespace and avoid production cache roots and keys.
- Notes that tiny-model, scripted or benchmark passes do not qualify full-model security or quality.

No threat-model assumption is invalidated and no new attack surface is introduced. The document makes no claims that contradict T-041 (TTL of 30 minutes, HMAC lookup tags, KEK wipe). I could not see the diff hunks or the rest of the file, so unchanged lines and the changed regions outside these excerpts are not examined. Later passes should check that the referenced tests and scripts actually exist, though that is a documentation-accuracy concern and not a security one.
